scenes.title: 1953 Imperial College Dual-Channel Audio Console: Shadowing the Right Ear Aloud While Missing English-to-German Switch in the Left Ear
scenes.era: 1953, Department of Electrical Engineering, Imperial College London

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1953 British acoustics & communications laboratory featuring a brushed-metal **dual-channel studio audio console** wired to **padded over-ear split-channel headphones**; above the console sit two crisp channel indicator boards — **Right Ear Channel: 'English Story (Shadowed Aloud: 99%)'** and **Left Ear Channel: '400Hz Beep / Pitch Shift = Noticed! | Switch to GERMAN = 0% Noticed!'**.

positions.who: Colin Cherry (mannequin in 1953 British tweed blazer, waistcoat, and striped tie)
positions.where: standing at the dual-channel studio audio console smoothly flipping the Left-Ear input toggle from English to German speech while monitoring the listener's unbroken shadowing

positions.who: Listener mannequin (wearing padded dual-channel studio headphones in 1953 knit jumper)
positions.where: speaking steadily into a desktop microphone repeating the Right-Ear English passage word-for-word — then shrugging in total surprise when asked if the Left Ear spoke German!

props.name: dual-channel studio audio console & padded over-ear headphones
props.period_detail: delivers independent Left vs Right speech streams cleanly

props.name: Left-Ear Test Toggle Board ('400Hz Tone [YES] | Male->Female Pitch [YES] | English->German [NO!]')
props.period_detail: contrasts noticed physical features against missed linguistic meaning
props.physical_behavior: crystallizes Broadbent's early filter data in one glance

actions.verb_sequence: shadows the Right-Ear English voice smoothly aloud -> Colin Cherry flips Left-Ear channel into German speech -> Listener never flinches and afterward reports 'Sounded like English' -> Cherry flips Left-Ear to a 400-Hz tone -> Listener immediately raises left hand!

reactions.reaction: laughs amazed at catching a beep instantly while missing an entire foreign language in the exact same ear
logs the birth of the 'Cocktail Party Problem'

scenes.wardrobe: 1953 British academic attire: warm wool tweed jacket, waistcoat, club tie; ribbed wool jumper over collared shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Switch the ignored headphone cup from a man's voice to a beep and they spot it instantly — switch English into German or backwards speech and they never notice a thing!

key_visual.description: a 1953 London acoustics lab where an engineer at a dual-channel studio audio console flips a Left-Ear German switch while a seated listener in padded headphones shadows the Right-Ear voice aloud

scenes.title: 1954 Ear-Hopping Speed Limit: 3 Switches Per Second Breaks Speech

layout.description: Bright bench with an electronic toggle switch hopping a single voice Left -> Right -> Left every 180 milliseconds.

positions.where: plotting the dramatic U-shaped dip in word recognition right around 3 alternations per second

props.name: Ear-Alternation Dip Graph ('180 ms Attention Switch Bottleneck')
props.period_detail: quantifies the physical time cost of toggling auditory focus

actions.verb_sequence: dials alternation rate to 3 Hz -> listener stumbles -> dials past 10 Hz -> intelligibility recovers

scenes.recognition_hook: Bounce one clear sentence back and forth between your two ears three times a second, and human comprehension crashes right on the 180-millisecond switch cost!

scenes.title: 2012 Awake Brain Decoding: Auditory Cortex Tunes Out the Crowd
scenes.era: 2012, UCSF human speech neurophysiology suite (Mesgarani & Chang)

layout.description: Clean high-key clinical display comparing a two-speaker mixed room spectrogram against the reconstructed neural spectrogram matching ONLY Speaker A.

positions.where: watching superior temporal cortex selectively amplify whichever speaker the listener chooses to follow

props.name: Mixed Audio vs Selective Cortical Reconstruction screen
props.period_detail: shows Cherry's 1953 filter operating live in human auditory cortex

actions.verb_sequence: shifts mental focus from Speaker 1 to Speaker 2 -> cortical spectrogram flips cleanly to Speaker 2

scenes.wardrobe: Modern white coat and casual shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Two voices hit your eardrum at identical volume — yet one synapse past primary hearing, your brain's electrical wave contains ONLY the voice you chose!

scenes.title: Protecting Your Single Verbal Channel in Everyday Work

layout.description: Tidy oak desk where a writer switches headphones from a talk podcast to calm instrumental audio before drafting a report.

positions.where: pausing spoken lyrics/talk and typing smoothly at full verbal clarity

props.name: Spoken-Word OFF / Instrumental ON toggle
props.period_detail: stops dichotic verbal competition while writing

actions.verb_sequence: switches off background talk show -> writing speed and recall double

scenes.recognition_hook: Never force your single verbal decoder to write sentences while another human voice talks in your headphones.
